In our assays, the wild-type P450  cam   exhibited a coupling efficiency of [unclassified numerical context withheld]% as judged by comparison of NADH consumption and 5-hydroxycamphor formation ( Table [unclassified numerical context withheld] ). The T252N and T252N/V253T mutants had coupling efficiencies of [unclassified numerical context withheld]% and [unclassified numerical context withheld]%, respectively ( Table [unclassified numerical context withheld] ). With none of these three enzymes was the formation of H [unclassified numerical context withheld] O [unclassified numerical context withheld]  detected, which suggests that the uncoupling occurred after oxygen activation to produce water. The T252A mutant, in contrast, exhibited a high rate of NADH consumption and the production of both H [unclassified numerical context withheld] O [unclassified numerical context withheld]  and H [unclassified numerical context withheld] O, but no camphor hydroxylation. molecule.display_text: [Mixed numerical source context retained; requested operand scope unresolved.]  The cytochrome P450 (CYP or P450) family of enzymes is involved in oxidative metabolism of a wide range of endo- and exogenous chemicals [ [unclassified numerical context withheld] ]. P450  cam   (CYP101) from  Pseudomonas putida , the structurally and biochemically best characterized P450 enzyme [ [unclassified numerical context withheld] ], catalyzes the regio- and stereospecific hydroxylation of camphor to [unclassified numerical context withheld]- exo -hydroxycamphor. As first established for P450  cam  , the general P450 catalytic cycle involves (a) substrate binding, (b) reduction of the iron from the ferric to the ferrous state, (c) oxygen binding to form the ferrous dioxy (Fe II -O [unclassified numerical context withheld] ) complex, (d) uptake of a second electron to give a ferric peroxy anion (Fe III -O [unclassified numerical context withheld]  − ) intermediate, (e) protonation to give the ferric hydroperoxy (Fe III -OOH) intermediate, (f) protonation of the distal oxygen in this complex with concurrent cleavage of the oxygen-oxygen bond, forming the activated (ferryl) oxidizing species, (g) insertion of the ferryl oxygen into the substrate, and (h) product release [ [unclassified numerical context withheld] ]. Uncoupled turnover, in which reducing equivalents are employed to reduce molecular oxygen to superoxide or H [unclassified numerical context withheld] O [unclassified numerical context withheld]  can occur by dissociation of the ligand from the ferrous dioxy or ferric hydroperoxide intermediates, respectively. Uncoupled turnover can also involve reduction of the ferryl catalytic species to water by the further uptake of electrons from the electron donor partner. The ferric hydroperoxy intermediate (step e) thus sits at an important branch point of P450 catalysis: dissociation of the hydroperoxy group results in uncoupled H [unclassified numerical context withheld] O [unclassified numerical context withheld]  production, whereas protonation and oxygen-oxygen bond cleavage leads to the productive oxidative pathway [ [unclassified numerical context withheld] ].

molecule.display_text: [Mixed numerical source context retained; requested operand scope unresolved.]  The cytochrome P450 (CYP or P450) family of enzymes is involved in oxidative metabolism of a wide range of endo- and exogenous chemicals [ [unclassified numerical context withheld] ]. P450  cam   (CYP101) from  Pseudomonas putida , the structurally and biochemically best characterized P450 enzyme [ [unclassified numerical context withheld] ], catalyzes the regio- and stereospecific hydroxylation of camphor to [unclassified numerical context withheld]- exo -hydroxycamphor. As first established for P450  cam  , the general P450 catalytic cycle involves (a) substrate binding, (b) reduction of the iron from the ferric to the ferrous state, (c) oxygen binding to form the ferrous dioxy (Fe II -O [unclassified numerical context withheld] ) complex, (d) uptake of a second electron to give a ferric peroxy anion (Fe III -O [unclassified numerical context withheld]  − ) intermediate, (e) protonation to give the ferric hydroperoxy (Fe III -OOH) intermediate, (f) protonation of the distal oxygen in this complex with concurrent cleavage of the oxygen-oxygen bond, forming the activated (ferryl) oxidizing species, (g) insertion of the ferryl oxygen into the substrate, and (h) product release [ [unclassified numerical context withheld] ]. Uncoupled turnover, in which reducing equivalents are employed to reduce molecular oxygen to superoxide or H [unclassified numerical context withheld] O [unclassified numerical context withheld]  can occur by dissociation of the ligand from the ferrous dioxy or ferric hydroperoxide intermediates, respectively. Uncoupled turnover can also involve reduction of the ferryl catalytic species to water by the further uptake of electrons from the electron donor partner. The ferric hydroperoxy intermediate (step e) thus sits at an important branch point of P450 catalysis: dissociation of the hydroperoxy group results in uncoupled H [unclassified numerical context withheld] O [unclassified numerical context withheld]  production, whereas protonation and oxygen-oxygen bond cleavage leads to the productive oxidative pathway [ [unclassified numerical context withheld] ].
